samples.question: The gray stroke in this picture is one single pipe. It never branches and never touches or crosses itself, so it has exactly two loose ends and you can follow it from one end to the other. A green disc covers one of the two loose ends; that is where you start. The pipe is built only from horizontal and vertical straight sections, so every bend in it is a right-angle turn. Imagine walking along the pipe from the green end, always facing the way you are travelling. At each bend you turn either toward your left hand or toward your right hand; left and right mean the walker's own left and right at that moment, which depends on the direction you were already heading, and not on any fixed side of the page. Number the bends 1, 2, 3, ... in the order you meet them as you walk from the green end. How long the sections are, how many bends there are in total, which way the other bends go, and where the pipe sits on the page do not matter; only the direction of the third bend counts. Walking from the green end, is the third bend a turn to your left or a turn to your right? Answer left or right.
